lead: The head is delivered but the shoulders do not follow with gentle downward traction, so extra manoeuvres are needed (or a head-to-body interval > 60 s). About 1 in 200 vaginal births; mostly unpredictable: about half occur in babies under 4 kg.
f: Shoulders stay antero-posterior: the anterior shoulder sticks behind the symphysis pubis · Rarely the posterior shoulder on the sacral promontory · A bony problem: episiotomy alone does not free it · Diabetes: large trunk, normal head · Each minute the fetal pH falls about 0.04; injury risk rises after 5 min
Antenatal: previous SD · macrosomia (EFW > 4 kg) · diabetes · BMI > 30 · post-term · Intrapartum: prolonged late 1st or 2nd stage · mid-cavity instrumental delivery · oxytocin augmentation, induction
Head delivers slowly; face and chin hard to deliver · Turtle sign: head retracts against the perineum · No restitution · Gentle axial traction fails

sc: Head out, retracts against the perineum, gentle traction fails → Shoulder dystocia: call help, McRoberts

f: Mother: PPH (commonest) · 3rd/4th degree, cervical and vaginal tears · uterine rupture (from fundal pressure) · symphysis separation · Baby: Erb palsy C5–C6 (commonest; waiter's tip, grasp present; under 10% permanent) · Klumpke C8–T1 (claw hand ± Horner) · fractured clavicle (no splint) or humerus · hypoxia, HIE, death

sc: Limp arm, waiter's tip, grasp present → Erb palsy (C5–C6)
Claw hand, ptosis, small pupil → Klumpke + Horner
tr: Plexus injury comes from strong lateral traction, not the manoeuvres; it can follow a normal birth or even a caesarean

f: Say "shoulder dystocia", note the time, stop her pushing · Help: midwives, obstetrician, anaesthetist, paediatrician · Evaluate for episiotomy (room for internal manoeuvres only) · Legs: McRoberts (hips hyperflexed onto the abdomen) · Pressure: suprapubic (Rubin I) from the fetal back side · Enter: Rubin II, Woods screw, reverse Woods · Remove the posterior arm · Roll onto all fours (Gaskin) · 30–60 s per manoeuvre · McRoberts + suprapubic pressure deliver about 80%

sc: Turtle sign; after calling for help, first manoeuvre → McRoberts
McRoberts and suprapubic pressure fail → Posterior arm or internal rotation
tr: Never fundal pressure: it impacts the shoulder and ruptures the uterus
Episiotomy is not the first step

f: Deliberate clavicle fracture · Zavanelli: head pushed back (terbutaline 0.25 mg SC), then caesarean · Symphysiotomy under local anaesthetic where theatre is far · Dead baby: cleidotomy

sc: All manoeuvres fail, theatre ready → Zavanelli + caesarean

f: Mother: expect PPH (active 3rd stage, oxytocin infusion); examine and repair the whole genital tract · Baby: paediatrician, cord gases (arterial pH < 7.20 = acidaemia), examine arms and clavicles · Document head and body times, anterior shoulder, each manoeuvre and who did it

Elective caesarean: EFW > 4.5 kg in a diabetic or > 5 kg in a non-diabetic woman · Diabetes: good control; planned birth 37+0 – 38+6 wk in pre-existing diabetes, by 40+6 wk in gestational diabetes (NICE; local units: 38–39 wk) · Previous SD recurs in about 1 in 10 · Known risk: deliver in hospital, no mid-cavity instrument · Scan weight can be wrong by 10–15%: every labour ward drills HELPERR

sc: Diabetic, EFW 4.6 kg before labour → Elective caesarean
GDM, EFW 4.2 kg, good control → Individual plan, not automatic caesarean
